chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud al-Sarri, who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the drinker of wine, 'Would he be given anything from the Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: Is a wine drinker eligible to receive Zakat?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Dawud al-Sarmi inquires whether a habitual wine drinker (sharib al-khamr) is eligible for Zakat, receiving a definitive negative response from the Imam. This ruling highlights the principle that while Zakat is for the poor and needy, specific moral transgressions can disqualify an individual, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that Zakat serves both as economic relief and a means of spiritual purification. The exclusion underscores the link between ritual purity, moral conduct, and the proper distribution of communal wealth.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Dawood Al Sarmy who said,
‘I asked himasws about the drinker of the wine, ‘Would he be given anything from the Zakāt?’ Heasws said: ‘no’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Dawud al-Sarmiy who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if Zakat can be given to one who consumes wine.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat cannot be given to such person.”
